latent_mechanisms.display_name: Explosive systemic HIV replication and plasma viremia
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Very early HIV replication in activated CD4 T cells produces high plasma HIV RNA, p24 antigenemia, transient CD4 decline, high infectivity, and seeds lymphoid, gut, liver, and CNS compartments.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Type I interferon and systemic inflammatory cytokine response
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Innate sensing of acute HIV viremia drives fever, headache, malaise, myalgia, modest CRP/ferritin elevation, anorexia, and a mononucleosis-like syndrome.
Acute antigenic stimulation expands lymph nodes and spleen and can generate atypical lymphocytes that mimic EBV infectious mononucleosis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Gut and mucosal CD4 T-cell depletion
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Early HIV preferentially infects activated CCR5+ mucosal CD4 T cells, especially in gut-associated lymphoid tissue, causing diarrhea, ulcer susceptibility, barrier injury, and rare severe intestinal bleeding.
Immune response to acute HIV produces maculopapular rash, mucosal ulcers, pharyngitis, and genital ulcers in a minority of patients.
Direct and immune-mediated hepatic injury during acute HIV can raise AST/ALT, occasionally with coagulopathy, while bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase may remain normal.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Early CNS seeding and lymphocytic aseptic meningitis
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: HIV enters the CNS early; compartmental replication and lymphocytic inflammation can produce severe headache, photophobia, meningismus, CSF mononuclear pleocytosis, elevated CSF protein, and rarely encephalitis.

Acute immune activation and marrow/reticuloendothelial effects can produce leukopenia or lymphocytosis, thrombocytopenia, atypical lymphocytes, hyperferritinemia, and rare HLH-like inflammatory presentations.
Rare immune neuropathy during seroconversion can produce Guillain-Barre syndrome with ascending weakness, cranial neuropathy, autonomic instability, respiratory failure, and sudden death.

mechanism_edges.rationale: Plasma HIV RNA is the direct measurement of acute systemic replication.
High viremia precedes or accompanies p24 antigen detection before full antibody maturation.
Acute infection can transiently lower circulating CD4 T-cell counts.
Cytokine release drives febrile ARS.
Reported fever is a common manifestation of acute HIV.
Systemic inflammatory signaling causes malaise and fatigue.
Myalgia is part of the acute retroviral flu-like syndrome.
Arthralgia often travels with the cytokine-driven ARS syndrome.
Headache is common in acute HIV and may be cytokine-driven even without meningitis.
CRP can be normal to moderately elevated, with occasional marked elevation in severe acute seroconversion.
Reactive lymphoid activation produces clinically detectable lymphadenopathy.
The intensity and extent of lymphadenopathy track reactive lymphoid expansion.
Reticuloendothelial activation can enlarge the spleen.
Acute HIV can mimic mononucleosis with atypical lymphocytes.
Gut mucosal infection and barrier disruption can cause diarrhea.
Gastrointestinal ARS can include nausea and vomiting.
Severe mucosal CD4 depletion and local inflammation can rarely manifest as colonic ulceration after exclusion of other pathogens.
A deep acute HIV-associated colonic ulcer can bleed substantially.
Maculopapular rash is a classic ARS sign.
When rash is described morphologically, ARS commonly has a diffuse maculopapular pattern.
Pharyngitis and odynophagia are frequent mucosal ARS symptoms.
Exudative pharyngitis is less specific but occurs in mononucleosis-like acute HIV presentations.
Mucosal ulcers can accompany acute HIV and also mark sexual transmission risk context.
Acute HIV hepatitis produces hepatocellular AST elevation.
Acute HIV hepatitis produces hepatocellular ALT elevation.
Severe acute hepatitis can impair synthetic function and raise INR.
Meningeal irritation causes photophobia.
Meningismus can occur in acute HIV aseptic meningitis.
Acute HIV meningitis produces mononuclear CSF pleocytosis.
CSF protein can rise with HIV-associated aseptic meningitis or meningoencephalitis.
CNS seeding creates the event state of aseptic meningitis or meningoencephalitis.

The disease range is deliberately broad because acute HIV can show leukopenia, normal WBC, or mononucleosis-like leukocytosis; this edge mainly gates WBC away from a healthy narrow background when the hematologic immune dysregulation mechanism is active.
Transient thrombocytopenia is a recognized acute HIV laboratory feature.
Inflammatory immune dysregulation can raise ferritin, rarely into HLH-like ranges.
GBS is a rare seroconversion complication.
Severe GBS can cause dysautonomia, arrhythmia, and sudden cardiac arrest.
Neurologic acute HIV presentations are uncommon but represent a more severe clinical form.
Mortality remains low unless hepatitis progresses to coagulopathy or multiorgan illness.
Rare severe GI ulcer bleeding or multiorgan presentations increase short-term hazard.

axes.shape_free_text: Absent before infection; during ARS usually very high, often above 100000 copies/mL and sometimes above 10000000 copies/mL, then falls toward a set point or rapidly suppresses after ART.
Often positive during the acute RNA-positive/antibody-negative or indeterminate window once viral load is high enough; may fade as antibodies mature or after ART.
Negative or indeterminate early, then evolves to full antibody reactivity over days to weeks; early ART can blunt or delay full serologic evolution.
Can transiently fall during ARS, sometimes below 500 and rarely near AIDS-range values, then partially rebounds as viremia declines or ART starts.
Fever commonly 38-39.5 C for several days to two weeks; exact temperature may be absent if only fever history is reported.
Reported fever when no measured temperature is available; often one of the main ARS anchors.
Normal to sinus tachycardia with fever, dehydration, pain, or bleeding; severe dysautonomia is rare and usually complication-driven.
Usually preserved in uncomplicated ARS; falls only with dehydration, hemorrhage, severe sepsis-like multiorgan illness, or dysautonomia.
Common constitutional symptom, often prominent and overlapping with malaise.
Diffuse myalgia is common in ARS and tracks the cytokine phase.
Arthralgia can accompany myalgia and fever; true inflammatory arthritis is uncommon.
Common headache from systemic ARS; severe headache with photophobia or CSF pleocytosis suggests aseptic meningitis.
Pharyngitis, odynophagia, or sore throat in the mononucleosis-like presentation.
Can be absent or present; exudative tonsillar pharyngitis makes ARS resemble EBV or streptococcal infection.
Maculopapular or morbilliform rash, often truncal and nonpruritic but variable; absence does not exclude ARS.
Morphologic satellite for diffuse maculopapular rash when source text specifies this pattern.
Genital or mucosal ulcer can occur during ARS or represent concomitant STI exposure context.
Cervical or generalized lymphadenopathy is common in ARS and anchors the child lymphadenopathy activity axis.
Severity, extent, and tenderness of lymphadenopathy when lymphadenopathy is present.
Splenomegaly is less common than lymphadenopathy but can appear in mononucleosis-like ARS.
Loose stools or diarrhea can reflect GI ARS; severe bloody diarrhea is unusual and should raise event hazard axes.
Vomiting or nausea can occur with GI/systemic ARS, dehydration, or hepatitis.
Photophobia is absent in uncomplicated ARS but rises with aseptic meningitis or meningoencephalitis.
Meningismus marker for CNS involvement; usually absent in uncomplicated ARS.
Normal without CNS disease; acute HIV aseptic meningitis usually has mild mononuclear pleocytosis.
Normal without CNS involvement; mild to moderate elevation with acute HIV aseptic meningitis.
Low overall; increased when severe headache, photophobia, neck stiffness, CSF pleocytosis, or CSF HIV RNA replication is present.
Can be low-normal, leukopenic, normal, or mononucleosis-like leukocytosis depending on timing and reactive lymphocytes.
Can be low, normal, or elevated with reactive mononucleosis-like presentations; interpret with WBC differential timing.
Atypical lymphocytes may be present in mononucleosis-like ARS but are not as defining as in EBV infectious mononucleosis.
Normal or mildly low in many cases; severe thrombocytopenia is unusual and suggests immune cytopenia or HLH-like complication.
Usually normal in uncomplicated ARS; falls with major bleeding or hemolytic/HLH-like complications.
Often normal to moderately elevated; marked CRP elevation can occur in severe acute seroconversion and is not automatically bacterial sepsis.
May rise with inflammation or acute hepatitis; very high values suggest HLH-like inflammatory complication or competing diagnoses.
Mild elevation is not uncommon; acute HIV hepatitis can produce AST in the hundreds, rarely more severe.
Mild elevation is not uncommon; acute HIV hepatitis can produce ALT in the hundreds while bilirubin may remain normal.
Usually normal in acute HIV hepatitis; elevation suggests cholestasis, hemolysis, severe hepatitis, or another cause.
Normally preserved; elevation indicates synthetic dysfunction or coagulopathy in severe hepatitis or systemic illness.
Usually normal; prolongation can appear with coagulopathy or anticoagulant exposure and should not be assumed core ARS.
Usually normal; rises with dehydration, rhabdomyolysis, drug toxicity, renal disease, or severe systemic illness.
Rare acute HIV GI complication after exclusion of common infectious causes; included because it is a documented acute HIV presentation, not a typical ARS requirement.
Usually absent; marked hematochezia indicates a GI bleeding event rather than routine ARS.
Near zero in ordinary ARS; rises when colonic ulceration and hematochezia are present.
Low in typical ARS; raised by observed severe GI bleeding, coagulopathy, thrombocytopenia, or procedure-related bleeding.
Rare seroconversion complication; should rise only with ascending weakness, areflexia, cranial neuropathy, or compatible CSF/electrophysiology.
Not a routine ARS feature; rises with severe GBS, shock, or major autonomic dysregulation.
Context axis for whether HIV RNA/p24/seroconversion evidence is available enough to start ART rapidly; not used as ordinary presentation evidence.
Context axis: recent CAB-LA PrEP can select INSTI resistance and changes empiric ART selection.
Context axis for transmitted or PrEP-associated integrase inhibitor resistance; should be driven by genotype or exposure history, not routine symptoms.
Treatment context axis because tenofovir plus FTC/3TC treats HBV, while stopping HBV-active ART can trigger hepatitis flare.
Treatment context axis; early HIV in pregnancy carries high perinatal transmission risk and changes drug-interaction/safety constraints.
Treatment context axis for low eGFR or severe kidney dysfunction affecting tenofovir, IVIG formulation choice, dosing, and toxicity monitoring; not a core ARS disease-course axis.
Event hazard for access-site or procedure-related bleeding during invasive hemostasis or line placement; driven by procedure exposure and coagulation status, not by uncomplicated ARS.

Short-term mortality is very low in uncomplicated ARS; increases with fulminant hepatitis/coagulopathy, severe meningoencephalitis, major GI bleeding, HLH-like inflammation, GBS dysautonomia, or delayed recognition of severe complications.
Oral thrush is a structured host-context clue for advanced cellular immunodeficiency or Candida overgrowth; it is not a disease-specific mechanism for this leaf.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Higher acute viremia is linked to greater transient CD4 depletion.
Sinus tachycardia tracks fever and systemic distress.
Constitutional symptoms fluctuate together during ARS.
Severe headache with photophobia should increase the CNS involvement state.
Mononuclear CSF pleocytosis makes aseptic meningitis materially more likely.
The satellite lymphadenopathy activity should only be consumed when the parent finding is present.
The maculopapular morphology satellite is meaningful only when rash is present.
Acute HIV hepatitis produces a hepatocellular transaminase pair.
Coagulopathy indicates severe hepatitis/systemic illness and raises short-term hazard.
A documented colonic ulcer is the substrate for ulcer bleeding hazard.
Observed hematochezia is direct evidence of major bleeding risk.
Life-threatening hemorrhage raises short-term mortality until hemostasis and resuscitation succeed.
Dysautonomia in GBS can cause arrhythmia or cardiac arrest.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Recent CAB-LA PrEP creates concern for integrase resistance and favors a boosted darunavir-containing regimen while genotype is pending.
Bictegravir activity is compromised by major INSTI resistance.
Tenofovir formulation and renal dosing/suitability depend on kidney function.

failure_modes: inability to maintain adherence during acute illness
drug interaction or renal constraint requiring regimen change

side_effects.interpretation: Small creatinine changes can occur from renal handling or tenofovir-related kidney effects; clinically meaningful toxicity is context dependent.
Nausea or GI intolerance can impair early adherence.

treatments.context_specific_role: Single-tablet rapid ART option for early HIV when INSTI resistance is not suspected; directly suppresses viral replication and secondarily resolves ARS inflammation.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Recent CAB-LA PrEP raises concern for INSTI resistance.
Dolutegravir activity is reduced by major INSTI resistance.
Tenofovir plus FTC or 3TC provides HBV-active therapy when HBV coinfection is present.

failure_modes: renal or bone constraints affecting tenofovir selection

side_effects.interpretation: Early GI intolerance can worsen nausea or vomiting.
Dolutegravir can raise creatinine by tubular secretion inhibition without true GFR decline; tenofovir toxicity is context dependent.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapid ART option using dolutegravir with a tenofovir backbone; suppresses acute HIV replication and reduces onward transmission risk.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Boosted darunavir is useful while genotype is pending when CAB-LA-associated INSTI resistance is plausible.
Cobicistat boosting should be avoided in pregnancy; ritonavir boosting and perinatal-specific regimen choice may be needed.

failure_modes: GI intolerance and pill burden impair adherence
protease inhibitor resistance is uncommon but possible

side_effects.interpretation: Boosted PI regimens can cause GI intolerance.
Darunavir is less bilirubin-raising than atazanavir but liver monitoring matters in acute hepatitis.

treatments.context_specific_role: High genetic barrier rapid ART pathway when integrase resistance is plausible or CAB-LA PrEP exposure complicates diagnosis.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: IVIG can worsen renal function depending on formulation and patient risk.
IVIG may be operationally favored over plasma exchange when bleeding or line-procedure risk is high.

failure_modes: benefit requires correct recognition of GBS rather than uncomplicated ARS
rapid dysautonomia or respiratory failure may still require ICU support
renal toxicity or thrombosis risk in susceptible hosts

side_effects.interpretation: IVIG-associated kidney injury is uncommon but clinically important.

treatments.context_specific_role: Complication-directed therapy for acute HIV-associated GBS; it does not directly suppress HIV replication and should be paired with ART when HIV is confirmed.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Hemostasis benefit is largest when active bleeding is present.
Coagulopathy increases rebleeding and procedure risk.

failure_modes: rebleeding despite embolization or endoscopic therapy

side_effects.interpretation: Procedural therapy carries access-site and procedure-related complication risk.

treatments.context_specific_role: Event-directed stabilization for rare acute HIV-associated colonic ulcer bleeding; it changes bleeding and mortality hazards but not HIV replication.

present.trajectory_modulation: Raises acute HIV prior when compatible fever, rash, pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy, diarrhea, cytopenia, or transaminitis occurs within the exposure window.
Raises prior and increases probability of high inoculum/high viremia presentation when source viremia is not suppressed.
Raises acquisition risk after exposure; does not independently intensify disease after infection.
May blunt or delay diagnostic markers and creates higher concern for INSTI resistance if breakthrough infection occurs.

treatment_effect_modulation.reason: CAB-LA pharmacokinetic tail can select INSTI resistance.
Boosted darunavir retains activity when INSTI resistance is uncertain.

present.trajectory_modulation: Does not define ARS phenotype but greatly increases perinatal transmission stakes during high viremia and changes ART safety constraints.
Increases ambiguity and hazard of acute hepatitis presentations; confirmatory HIV tests should remain separate from presentation observations.
Prolongs high viremia, symptoms, transmission risk, and time for rare severe complications to declare themselves.
Raises exposure prior and can create overlapping mucocutaneous findings.

supportive_care.clinical_role: Reduces symptom burden and dehydration while ART suppresses viral replication; does not directly change HIV replication.
Genotype, HIV RNA, CD4, hepatitis serologies, renal/liver labs, and pregnancy testing guide safe rapid ART and monitoring.
Lumbar puncture, neuroimaging, empiric exclusion of bacterial/HSV etiologies, and close neurologic follow-up when severe headache or meningismus is present.
IV access, fluids, blood products, hemostasis, and monitoring stabilize rare severe GI bleeding while etiologic HIV treatment proceeds.
Counsel condoms or abstinence until sustained viral suppression, test and offer prevention to partners, and link to HIV care.
